title: Integrated Pathology and Pharmacology Reasoning
subject: INI-CET Strategy
preview: Pathology gives the structural or molecular lesion; pharmacology links that lesion to a therapeutic target.
quickRevision: Pathology gives the structural or molecular lesion; pharmacology links that lesion to a therapeutic target.
Predict a mechanism-linked adverse effect rather than memorizing unrelated side-effect lists.
Use the patient's comorbidities and drug interactions when comparing two plausible agents.

sections.title: Recognize the question type
points: Pathology gives the structural or molecular lesion; pharmacology links that lesion to a therapeutic target.
Identify the relevant receptor, enzyme, pathway or cell before choosing a drug effect.

sections.title: Use this in timed practice
points: Predict a mechanism-linked adverse effect rather than memorizing unrelated side-effect lists.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Avoid treating every drug in one class as identical in selectivity or adverse-effect profile.

quiz.question: Which concept helps integrate pathology with pharmacology?
options: Grouping all diseases by age alone
Linking disease mechanism to drug target
quiz.explanation: Linking disease mechanism to drug target. Pathology gives the structural or molecular lesion; pharmacology links that lesion to a therapeutic target.
